items.title: NASA Researcher: "the better automation gets, the worse the problem gets"
items.summary: If you want to find out which parts of your job are at risk from AI, try my free one-page task audit: https://ai-survivalguide.com/taskaudit In 2009, the autopilot on Air France 447 switched off and handed the plane back to a crew that rarely flew by hand at that altitude. Four minutes and twenty-three seconds later, all 228 people on board were dead. items.title: The Humans Who Train Frontier AI ( Ep. 1048 with Gabe Greenberg)
items.summary: In Episode #1048, Gabe Greenberg (Founder and CEO of G2i) joins @JonKrohnLearns to describe the human labour behind frontier AI. G2i grew from a one-person shop to $15 million in revenue with no VC backing, and its bench of 8,000 vetted engineers now builds the reinforcement learning data and environments that frontier labs train on; over the past year G2i paid those engineers $50 million. Three years ago the work could be done by thousands of junior engineers at $20 to $40 an hour, and today it takes staff-level experts commanding $200 to $300. In this episode, Gabe explains what changed, why SWE-bench and its successors saturated into uselessness, what fidelity an RL environment has to reach before it improves a model, and how G2i's own agentic platform has written tens of millions of lines of production code. items.title: Supervised, Unsupervised, Classification & Regression: The Building Blocks of Prediction
items.summary: How a model learns depends on whether your data comes with answers attached. Four terms cover almost every machine learning model built. Terms covered: - Supervised Learning: training on labeled data where both input and correct output are known, so the model learns patterns it can apply to cases it has never seen - Unsupervised Learning: no labels, no predefined categories. The model explores the data and finds natural groupings and structures on its own. - Classification: predicting which category something belongs to. Churn or stay, fraudulent or legitimate, benign or malignant. - Regression: predicting a continuous numerical value. A sale price, next month's inventory need, a customer's projected lifetime value. Supervised or unsupervised, classification or regression.
